title: Spotter: Let the Embodied Model Lead, and the VLM Reflect for It
abstract: arXiv:2609.36808v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Current embodied models do not respond to their own failures, although what just went wrong could inform a small adjustment on the next attempt, the kind of reflection behind the gains of thinking in language models. We test whether they can repair a known error, which requires producing a correction and judging whether it is right. Stopped at a failure and allowed to retry, they seldom repair it through their own randomness or from a language description of the error, and best-of-N selection cannot pick the successful candidate after a failure. We attribute this to training only on successful demonstrations and to inputs too narrow to show what went wrong, and conclude that reflection must come from a vision-language model (VLM), which takes in far more information, such as the episode history and text, and is more general. translated_title: Spotter：让具身模型主导，VLM为其反思
translated_abstract: 当前的具身模型不会对自身的失败做出响应，尽管刚才出现的问题本可以指导下一次尝试时的小幅调整——这种反思能力正是语言模型中“思考”带来收益的机制。我们测试了它们能否修复已知错误，这需要产出修正方案并判断其是否正确。实验表明，在遭遇失败并允许重试时，这些模型很少能通过自身的随机性或错误的语言描述来修复错误，而且best-of-N选择在失败后也无法选出成功的候选方案。我们将这一现象归因于模型仅在成功演示上进行训练，且输入过于狭窄而无法呈现问题所在，并得出结论：反思必须由视觉语言模型（VLM）来完成，因为VLM能够接收远为丰富的信息（例如回合历史和文本），且更具通用性。此前由VLM主导的工作让VLM规划每一步操作，并将具身模型作为工具来调用，把VLM置于关键路径上。
tldr: 提出Spotter框架，让具身模型保持主导执行，而由视觉语言模型（VLM）在失败时进行反思并协助修正，从而解决现有具身模型无法从自身错误中恢复的问题。
en_tdlr: Spotter lets the embodied model lead while a VLM reflects on its failures and guides corrections, enabling error repair that embodied models cannot achieve on their own.
